 Ty Jerome (hip) is probable to play against the Timberwolves on Saturday.
 Jerome is expected to be back following a four-game absence. That should push Cam Spencer back to the bench, but with Javon Small out due to personal reasons, Spencer should still play a large role.

 Javon Small 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #10 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Javon Small (personal) has been ruled out against the Timberwolves on Saturday. 
 Small has been an important reserve for Memphis this season, especially as of late. With Ty Jerome expected to return from a four-game absence, Small’s minutes will go to Cam Spencer, who filled in nicely as a starter with Jerome out. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome (hip) is out for Thursday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Jerome will miss a fourth straight game with a right hip impingement. Cam Spencer has played well as his replacement in the starting lineup and should probably be rostered in some 12-team leagues even after Jerome returns. 
 Cam Spencer 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #24 
 Cam Spencer finished Wednesday’s win over the Cavaliers with 26 points (9-of-11 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), one rebound, seven assists, one block and five three-pointers. 
 Making another start for the injured Ty Jerome, Spencer led the Grizzlies in points and assists as the team moved to 8-0 on the road this season. While the former UConn guard had a quiet fourth quarter, he scored 13 of his 26 points in the third, shooting 5-of-5 from the field and hitting three three-pointers. At a minimum, Spencer needs to be rostered until Jerome is healthy enough to play. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome (hip) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Jerome’s hip injury will sideline him for a third straight game, meaning the Grizzlies will once again rely on Cam Spencer at point guard. He’s worth rostering until Jerome returns. In deeper leagues, Javon Small may be worth a look after recording his first double-double in Monday’s win over the Wizards. 
 Cam Spencer 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #24 
 Cam Spencer accumulated 12 points (4-of-10 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), six rebounds, nine assists and one three-pointer in Monday’s win over the Grizzlies. 
 Making a second straight start for the injured Ty Jerome (hip), Spencer finished Monday’s victory one assist shy of a double-double. In Memphis’ wins over the Nets and Wizards, he totaled 17 assists and four turnovers. Clearly, Spencer’s fantasy ceiling will depend on Jerome’s availability. However, he’s played well enough to merit being rostered in deep leagues even after the Grizzlies get their starting point guard back. 
 Cam Spencer 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #24 
 Cam Spencer, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey will start Monday’s game against the Wizards. 
 Edey is back after a two-game absence and will start, returning to his usual starting center role. However, the Grizzlies remain without Ty Jerome (hip), so Spencer starts again at point guard and is worth streaming.

 Ty Jerome (hip) is out for Monday’s game against the Wizards. 
 Jerome will miss a second straight game due to a sore right hip. Cam Spencer played well in his absence on Saturday, recording 17 points, eight assists and three three-pointers. He is worth streaming in this spot, especially for managers needing assist production. 
 Cam Spencer 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #24 
 Cam Spencer started on Saturday and finished with 17 points (6-of-10 FGs), one rebound, eight assists, two steals and three three-pointers against the Nets. 
 Spencer got the starting nod with Ty Jerome (hip) sidelined for this game, and he took advantage of the opportunity. In his other start this season, he had a season-high 13 assists. He was able to drop plenty of dimes in this one, but he also set a new season high for points and scored in double figures for a third straight game. He has been an excellent reserve this year, but he should be considered a super streamer when Jerome is out of the lineup.

 With Ty Jerome (hip) sidelined for the second leg of this back-to-back, Spencer will get the starting nod. Spencer dished out 13 assists in his only other start this season and should be worth streaming.

 Darryn Peterson puts up 20 points (7-of-20 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), ten rebounds, eight assists, two steals, and a block in the loss to the Suns on Friday. 
 Darryn was more on the ball in this game and it showed. He got his first career double-double and he wasn’t that far off from a triple-double. He was running the offense a lot of the time, that led to the high assists numbers. He did a good job attacking the glass and attacking on the offensive end. Since the injuries to Lauri Markkanen, Darryn has gotten more confident and looking much better. Continue to hold and enjoy what he’s giving you.

 Keyonte George got himself 14 points (4-of-17 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, and four turnovers in the 111-101 loss to the Suns on Friday. 
 He didn’t have the most efficient night in this one but still gave you some good assists. Considering the performances he’s had the past couple games; you’ll take a bad one every now and then. The next opportunity for Keyonte to bounce back will be against the Mavericks on Sunday.

 Jaxson Hayes 
 UTA 
 Center-Forward 
 #11 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Jaxson Hayes had 18 points (7-of-8 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs) and 14 rebounds in the loss to the Suns. 
 Hayes was productive tonight and did a good job finishing around the rim through contact. He rebounded the ball well and did a solid job ending possessions. He’s useful as a streamer, but there’s not much consistency with any of the Jazz bigs. On top of that, Jusuf Nurkic will be re-evaluated in one week, and was active in warmups, so it won’t be long until Nurkic is added into the rotation. He also did land on his hip in the fourth quarter. He stayed in the game, but it’s possible he pops back up on the injury report.

 Devin Booker put up 23 points (9-of-22 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, and a three in the 111-101 win over the Jazz on Friday. 
 Booker got going in the third quarter to help the Suns maintain the lead when the Suns offense stalled. He didn’t have the most efficient night, or get many peripheral stats, but he’s had a good past few games, so it’s hard to complain. The Suns next play against the Pelicans on Monday.

 Miles Bridges had 18 points (7-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds, four assists, a steal, a block, and a three in the win over the Jazz. 
 Bridges did a good job taking advantage of the Jazz defense by taking a lot of high percentage looks. He crashed the glass and gave the Jazz issues all night. On the season, Bridges has been marginally disappointing, since the numbers are down, but he’s on a better team. The role is secure on this Suns team and barring injuries, it isn’t likely that his offensive load will increase.

 Paul Reed provided a boost off the bench with eight points (3-of-5 FGs), seven rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block against the Raptors on Friday.
 Reed’s value has been capped since he moved to the bench in favor of Daniss Jenkins, but there have still been a few games where he has played more minutes than John Collins, who has been starting at center lately. This was one of those games, with Reed playing 28 minutes to Collins’ 20. Until Jalen Duren (hamstring) returns, J.B. Bickerstaff will likely continue to roll with the hot hand at center, which will make it frustrating to roster both Reed and Collins most of the time.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Kevin Huerter lit up the Raptors with 20 points (7-of-15 FGs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers on Friday.
 This was Huerter’s third straight game as a starter with Duncan Robinson sidelined, and this was his best performance during this stretch. He had his third 20-point performance of the season and matched his season high for triples. Robinson should miss at least 1-2 more games, which means Huerter should continue to start. As long as he’s starting, Huerter should be considered a must-roster player.
 -  Noah Rubin 
 Recap

 Cade Cunningham 
 DET 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Player Stats

 Cade Cunningham returned to the lineup on Friday and finished with 23 points (10-of-22 FGs), five rebounds, nine assists, one steal and two three-pointers in a 105-102 loss to the Raptors.
 Cunningham was back after sitting out on Wednesday against New Orleans, but that wasn’t enough to get the Pistons a third straight win. He came close to recording his third double-double of the season, but this wasn’t a great performance to Cunningham’s standards. They’ll wrap this week up in Atlanta on Sunday, and they’ll need Cunningham to be much better than he was in this game to get the win.
 -  Noah Rubin 
 Recap 
 More Cade Cunningham News
 Immanuel Quickley 
 TOR 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Immanuel Quickley recorded a double-double on Friday with 18 points (6-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, 11 assists and three three-pointers against the Pistons.
 Quickley has had a strong season, but he hasn’t been able to step up as a playmaker like he did in this one. He recorded his first double-double of the year and set a new season high for assists. With Kawhi Leonard (knee) and RJ Barrett (hamstring) both sidelined, Quickley’s offense is more important than ever for Toronto. He’ll look to stay hot in their next game against the Bucks on Monday.
 -  Noah Rubin
